title: Dice, Gutters, Leading, Ink & Markers
description: Five jobs the platform just took back from JavaScript: random values, gap rules, leading trim, automatic ink and generated carousel furniture.

drops.title: Randomness, Declared
drops.description: A confetti field, an equaliser and a scatter plot whose every delay, hue and size is rolled by CSS itself.
drops.concept: random(min, max) gives each element its own value without a line of JavaScript writing inline styles. A leading dashed ident caches one roll so several declarations on the same element agree; the element-shared keyword makes every match agree instead; a trailing third argument quantises the result to a step. The demo rolls four values per element and feeds them to position, hue, size, duration and delay.
drops.source: Chris Coyier · Frontend Masters blog (with WebKit's implementation notes)

interaction.mouse: Sliders change population, spread and tempo across all three fields at once.
interaction.click: “Roll again” rebuilds the elements, which draws a fresh set of values.
interaction.touch: Same controls; the panel stacks above the demos on narrow screens.

drops.title: Rules in the Gaps
drops.description: column-rule and the new row-rule paint dividers down the middle of grid and flex gutters — spanning tiles included.
drops.concept: Gap decorations put the divider inside the gap instead of on the item. A grid or flex container takes column-rule and row-rule with border-like shorthand, the rule is centred in the gutter and never widens it, and rule-break decides what happens where rules cross. The demo runs the same two declarations over a bento grid with spanning tiles, a settings list and a wrapping flex row.
drops.source: Chrome developer blog — “Gap decorations: Now available in Chromium”

interaction.mouse: Gap, rule width, hue and line style are live; the rules re-measure as the grid reflows.
interaction.click: The style select switches between solid, dashed, dotted and double.
interaction.touch: The bento grid drops to two columns and the rules follow.

drops.title: Trim the Leading
drops.description: text-box-trim cuts the half-leading off a heading's box, so equal padding finally looks equal.
drops.concept: Every line box carries the font's ascent above the cap height and its descent below the baseline, which is why headings never sit where you put them. text-box-trim removes it and text-box-edge says which metrics to cut back to. Firefox 154 was the last engine to ship the pair. Three side-by-side comparisons show the same type with and without the trim, with the boxes drawn in.
drops.source: web.dev platform digest — “New to the web platform in August”

interaction.mouse: Type size, over edge and under edge are live on every trimmed element.
interaction.click: “Show the box” toggles the dashed outline of the text box itself.

drops.title: The Colour Decides the Ink
drops.description: Drag a hue slider and every label flips between black and white on its own — no parallel map of text colours.
drops.concept: contrast-color() takes the background you already declared and returns whichever of black or white reads better against it. That means a brand colour can arrive from a database, a theme picker or a slider, and the label on top stays legible without anyone maintaining a lookup table. Four instances — buttons, a twelve-hue wheel, an eleven-step lightness ramp and transit line badges — all flip live.

interaction.mouse: Hue, saturation and lightness sliders retint every instance at once.
interaction.click: “Sweep the hue” animates the whole wheel so you can watch the flip point travel.
interaction.touch: Ramp and strip collapse to six columns; sliders work the same.

drops.title: A Carousel With No Script
drops.description: ::scroll-button() arrows that disable themselves, ::scroll-marker dots for every child, :target-current for the live one.
drops.concept: The arrows and the dots were the only reason a carousel ever needed a library. A scroll container can now generate up to four buttons that know when they have reached an end, a marker per child, and a group to lay the markers out in; :target-current styles whichever marker matches the current scroll position. Keyboard focus and snap behaviour come free because it is still just a scroller.

interaction.mouse: Click the generated arrows or any dot; the dot for the centred item lights up.
interaction.click: Dot size, button size and accent hue are live across all three carousels.
interaction.touch: Swipe each rail — the markers track the scroll position.
